definition: To start a meeting, project or event.
exampleSentence: Let us kick off the meeting with a quick update from each team.

definition: To finish something.
exampleSentence: We have five minutes left, so let us wrap up the discussion.

definition: To introduce a new product or system, often step by step.
exampleSentence: The company will roll out the new app to all users in April.

definition: To give responsibility or work to someone else.
exampleSentence: Before your holiday, please hand over your tasks to a colleague.

definition: To prepare a written document.
exampleSentence: Our lawyer will draw up the contract this week.

definition: To end people's jobs because there is not enough work or money.
exampleSentence: The factory had to lay off fifty workers last year.

definition: To leave an important position.
exampleSentence: The CEO decided to step down after ten years in the job.

definition: To give final approval.
exampleSentence: The director must sign off on the budget before we can start.

definition: To write or enter your details to use a system or building.
exampleSentence: Visitors must sign in at the reception desk.

definition: To quickly practice or explain something.
exampleSentence: Let us run through the presentation once more before the client arrives.

definition: To complete something you started or promised.
exampleSentence: Making plans is easy; the hard part is to follow through.

definition: To look at data in more detail.
exampleSentence: The dashboard lets managers drill down into sales by region.

definition: To increase the size or amount of something.
exampleSentence: We need to scale up our servers before the big sale.

definition: To reduce spending or an amount.
exampleSentence: The company had to cut back on travel to save money.

definition: To introduce something new, or to earn money.
exampleSentence: The new product will bring in a lot of new customers.

definition: To remove something, such as a website or a post.
exampleSentence: We had to take down the website for a few hours to fix it.

definition: To suggest an idea or plan for discussion.
exampleSentence: Anyone can put forward an idea at our monthly meeting.

definition: To explain something clearly, often in writing.
exampleSentence: This document will set out the rules for working from home.

definition: To choose not to take part in something.
exampleSentence: Customers can opt out of marketing emails at any time.

definition: To contact someone, often to offer or ask for help.
exampleSentence: Feel free to reach out if you have any questions.

definition: To include someone in a discussion or email.
exampleSentence: Please loop in the legal team before we sign anything.

definition: To return to a topic later.
exampleSentence: We are out of time, so let us circle back to this tomorrow.

definition: To solve small problems.
exampleSentence: We still need to iron out a few details in the contract.

definition: To slowly stop using something.
exampleSentence: The company plans to phase out paper invoices by next year.

definition: To fail to do something as fast as planned.
exampleSentence: If we lose another developer, we will fall behind schedule.

definition: To fail to happen.
exampleSentence: The deal might fall through if we cannot lower the price.

definition: To make a failing business successful.
exampleSentence: The new CEO managed to turn around the struggling company.

definition: To do someone's work while they are away.
exampleSentence: Can you cover for me while I am at the doctor?

definition: To take someone's place for a short time.
exampleSentence: Maria will stand in for the manager at today's meeting.

definition: To have someone as your manager.
exampleSentence: In this role, you will report to the head of IT.

definition: To stop using a computer system.
exampleSentence: Always log off before you leave your desk at night.

definition: To delay something.
exampleSentence: Problems with the supplier may hold up the delivery.

definition: To contact someone briefly to report or ask about progress.
exampleSentence: I will check in with you on Friday to see how it is going.

definition: To read or check something quickly.
exampleSentence: Could you look over my email before I send it to the client?

definition: To spend time doing or improving something.
exampleSentence: I am going to work on the new design all afternoon.

definition: To use an amount of time or space.
exampleSentence: Meetings take up too much of my working day.

definition: To trust someone to do something.
exampleSentence: You can count on me to finish the report on time.

definition: To spend time or effort on something.
exampleSentence: She is willing to put in extra hours when the team needs help.

definition: To make time, money or space available.
exampleSentence: Automating reports will free up time for more important work.

definition: To finish or survive something difficult.
exampleSentence: We have a lot of emails to get through before lunch.
